title: Representative coherence data for derived tensor on a ringed site
statement: Let $J$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the ordinary signed total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex], and the recorded derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Fix a closed monoidal structure [def-sfb-monoidal-category] $S$ for that internal Hom, its canonical simultaneous K-flat tensor model $T$ [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], and a symmetric structure $\beta$ on $S$. Define the coefficient unit complex to be the actual complex $\mathcal O[0]$, with its degree-zero section induced by the single-complex identification. A representative coherence datum consists of: (1) for every pair $(P,Q)$ with at least one K-flat factor, an isomorphism $Q(\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q))\cong S(QP,QQ)$; (2) agreement with $T$ when both factors are K-flat, and naturality in all chain maps between allowed pairs; (3) an isomorphism from the monoidal unit to $Q(\mathcal O[0])$; (4) realization of $\beta$ on every simultaneous K-flat model by the chain isomorphism sending a summand $x\otimes y$ of bidegree $(p,q)$ to $(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$; (5) realization of the associator on triples of K-flat models by sign-free reassociation of pure-tensor summands; (6) realization of the left and right unitors on every K-flat model by multiplication by the degree-zero scalar. In (4)-(6) the realizing chain isomorphisms must commute after localization with the fixed tensor comparison and, for the unitors, the fixed unit isomorphism. These are data and equations defining the notion, not an assertion that such data exist. Site object, arrow, coefficient and localization universes remain independent, with module universe $\max(c,v,u)$.
